title: Required PostgreSQL suites (strict; independent of the commerce reliability gate): PostgreSQL proofs plus runner/fixture regressions
rules: Every node id below must be collected and must pass; a skip, failure, error, missing or uninventoried collection fails the run.
The required_env of a suite must be present (and equal, where a value is given) before pytest starts; otherwise the runner exits 2 without running anything.

kind is 'proof' for the PostgreSQL proofs themselves and 'runner_regression' for regressions of the runner and the shared fixture; the verdict counts them separately, and both kinds are required. Any other kind is rejected before anything runs.
This inventory carries no allowances. It does not measure the commerce reliability gate; that gate's acceptance remains a separate result.

Adding or removing a test in a listed module is a reviewed change to this inventory; the self-test compares it with pytest's own collection, so a stale inventory fails instead of silently omitting a test.

suites.origin: Agent loop PR — dormant agent loop core and its durable guarantees: one turn through reasoning, read-only fixture tools and observations feeding the next decision; durable ownership- and revision-guarded attempt debits with concurrency arbitration and re-entry restoration; enforced provider and tool waits with the deadline re-checked inside the reservation transaction; scope, eligibility and ownership boundaries; complete provider-result validation; isolation of authoritative schemas and context; closed ownership-loss outcomes; repeat policy: duplicates inside one bundle refused before the first tool runs, and a durable crash-safe recovery allowance of one original attempt plus one repeat

Pilot integration PR — the owner pilot end to end on real PostgreSQL with the real admission, ownership, agent loop, Anthropic adapter, trusted read context and delivery ledger, and only the model's HTTP call and the WhatsApp transport scripted: one inbound message answered at most once (redelivery, re-entry reusing the reserved intent, two concurrent invocations sending once), never a success the send does not support (rejected, unknown, a transport that raises, a provider failure, a model refusal, a draft citing unobserved evidence), no blind retry of an uncertain send, a follow-up answered from the conversation the platform already recorded, tenant and conversation scope, and refusal when the runtime schema is not present
PR #1099 — revision 0111: the handover's durable barrier, worker fleet and deferred inbound, created from the package's own metadata, refused rather than reconciled on a mismatch, and reversible

PR #1099 — the two handover controls the closure review reproduced: a previously selected invocation admitting after a zero-count settlement check, and a new response while an abandoned runtime send completes
Trial evidence collector: repository-written turns, exact tenant/live scope, resolved accounting, read-only consistent snapshot and independent concurrent completion
pilot follow-up: the re-runnable, secret-free synthetic probe of the runtime pilot

Runner PR — explicit-target authority at the shared fixture's connection boundary (R1): an unreachable explicit URL fails the proof with no fallback and no test database on an alternate service; a reachable explicit URL is used while every alternate is dead

Salla address-candidate PR — revision 0110 (fresh, create_all reconciliation, reversible), candidate durability across commit/session/conversation, one provenance row per address, tenant isolation, selected-address reuse after reset, and the independent review's PostgreSQL closure: evidence absent before commit / present after / gone after rollback, two concurrent first imports committing one address, an absent provenance table still committing the confirmed address, and a concurrent refresh between offer and selection being refused
